sections.h2: Where is Columbia, SC, and what is special about its location?
sections.html:
Columbia is the capital of South Carolina and the county seat of Richland County, with parts of the city reaching into Lexington and Kershaw counties. It sits near the center of the state at the fall line, where the Piedmont meets the Atlantic Coastal Plain.

The Broad and Saluda rivers meet here to form the Congaree River. That geography shaped the city, and it still matters for anyone selling a house close to the water.

sections.h2: How did Columbia become the capital, and why does it matter for houses?
sections.html:
Columbia was South Carolina's first planned capital. The General Assembly approved the site on March 22, 1786, and surveyor John Guignard laid out a grid two miles on a side, five years before the plan for Washington, D.C.

Union forces under Sherman captured the city on February 17, 1865, and much of it burned that night and the next day. Modern historians conclude Sherman did not order the fire. The result is a city with a planned core, a mix of surviving and rebuilt neighborhoods, and housing from many eras.

That mix is why a Columbia seller can own anything from a historic bungalow to a postwar ranch. The condition issues differ a lot from one street to the next, so a buyer's price is rarely a citywide number.

sections.h2: Which neighborhoods and areas make up Columbia?
sections.html:
Columbia has many named neighborhoods, each with its own housing stock and buyer base. Names listed for the city include:

  • Arsenal Hill and Congaree Vista near downtown
  • Elmwood Park and Waverly Historic District
  • Five Points, Old Shandon and University Hill, close to the university
  • Granby Mill Village and Rosewood

Most of the city is served by Richland County School District One. Parts of the city that fall in Lexington or Kershaw counties are handled by those counties for property records, so check which county your parcel is in before you call an office.

sections.h2: What employers and institutions drive Columbia's housing demand?
sections.html:
State government, the University of South Carolina and Fort Jackson are among the largest employers in Columbia. The University of South Carolina is the state's flagship, with more than 30,000 students on the Columbia campus.

Healthcare and insurance add steady jobs through Prisma Health Midlands and BlueCross BlueShield of South Carolina. Manufacturing names include Michelin, Honeywell, Westinghouse Electric and FN Herstal. Allen University, Benedict College, Columbia College, Columbia International University and Midlands Technical College are also in the city.

Sellers of rental houses near the campuses or downtown should expect buyers to ask about tenants and rental permits, which the section on rentals below covers.

sections.h2: What is the weather like in Columbia, and what does it mean for a roof or HVAC?
sections.html:
Columbia has a humid subtropical climate with hot, humid summers and mild winters. The record high is 113 degrees Fahrenheit, set on June 29, 2012, and the record low is minus 2 degrees on February 14, 1899. Snow averages only about 1.2 inches a year.

Long, hot summers put the load on air conditioning, attic ventilation and roofing, so inspectors here pay close attention to those.

Because the city sits on the fall line, with rivers that meet downstream, ask for a flood zone determination on any parcel near the Broad, Saluda or Congaree rivers.

sections.h2: How do you get around Columbia, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Columbia is served by four interstates: I-20 running east and west, I-26 running northwest to southeast, I-77 running north toward Rock Hill and Charlotte, and I-126 linking downtown to I-26 and I-20. Columbia Metropolitan Airport has service from American Eagle, Delta Connection and United Express, and Amtrak's Silver Star stops in the city daily.

A smaller airfield, Jim Hamilton-L.B. Owens Airport, handles general aviation in Rosewood. Good road access is a real selling point for a Columbia house, and a house near an interstate ramp or a rail line should be described honestly to buyers, since noise comes up in showings.

sections.h2: What rules cover rentals in Columbia?
sections.html:
Every residential rental in the City of Columbia needs a Residential Rental Permit before it is occupied as a rental. The requirement applies to units rented after July 1, 2016, and permits expire each year on December 31.

  • Owners of up to 4 units use the nonbusiness form, and owners of 5 or more use the business form.
  • Applications go to the Code Enforcement Division at 920 Hemlock Drive, Columbia, SC 29201, and payment is made online after approval.
  • The contact listed for questions is 803-545-4362.

Short-term rentals have their own rules. Operating one needs an STR Permit from Code Enforcement and a Business License. Under Ordinance 2025-107, STRs are allowed in mixed-use, activity center and corridor, commercial and employment campus districts. In residential districts they are allowed on parcels fronting a four-lane arterial or collector street. An ordinance approved March 3, 2026 lets owner-occupied homes in residential districts operate without the four-lane requirement. See the city's STR page and the residential rentals page.

sections.h2: How do property tax bills and appeals work for a Columbia house?
sections.html:
In South Carolina, county governments levy and collect property tax, and the Richland County Assessor sets values for houses inside Columbia. Taxes are due between September 30 and January 15, and penalties follow in steps: 3 percent after January 15, another 7 percent if still unpaid by February 2, and another 5 percent by March 17 (Code sections 12-45-70 and 12-45-180).

To contest a value in Richland County, file a written objection with the Assessor, online or in person, with documents that support your number. The deadline is 90 days from the dated reassessment notice, or the first penalty date on the current bill, whichever comes first. A representative needs a power of attorney on Form SC2848, and an LLC needs to provide its organizing documents.

The Assessor's Office is at 2020 Hampton Street, Suite 2058, Columbia, SC 29204, phone 803-576-2640. The county's assessment appeal page has the online portal. We did not find a confirmed reassessment year on that page, so ask the office.

sections.h2: What options do Columbia sellers have for a quick sale?
sections.html:
A Columbia seller can list with an agent, sell without one, or accept a cash offer. Houses near the university or downtown often attract investors, while houses in need of work or with tenants in place are harder to sell on the open market.

Before you decide, gather the permit status of any rental, the parcel's county, the tax bill, and your mortgage payoff. Those four items answer most of the questions a buyer or closing attorney will ask.

faqs.a: Yes. Columbia is the seat of Richland County, but parts of the city extend into Lexington and Kershaw counties. Check your parcel's county before contacting an assessor or treasurer.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental permit to sell a rented house in Columbia?
faqs.a: The city requires a Residential Rental Permit for every rental unit, renewed each year by December 31. A buyer will want to see that it is current. Ask Code Enforcement at 803-545-4362 if you are unsure.

faqs.q: When are Richland County property taxes due?
faqs.a: State law makes taxes payable between September 30 and January 15. A 3 percent penalty follows after January 15, so ask the treasurer for your exact notice date and amount.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Columbia assessment?
faqs.a: Richland County allows 90 days from the dated reassessment notice, or until the first penalty date on the current bill, whichever comes first. Filing an appeal does not replace paying the bill.

faqs.q: Can a buyer use a Columbia house as an Airbnb?
faqs.a: Only if zoning and the city permit allow it. The city requires an STR Permit and a Business License. Residential locations depend on the street or on owner occupancy under the 2026 ordinance.
